title: Signal: link.reconnect is a no-op after a boot-time daemon failure; backend stuck half-connected
description: Observed 2026-11-06 on the user's install (megachatd elegant-cray 3c15fce, log /tmp/signal-tui.log). Sequence: server starts with signal.enabled=true and signal.user_number set but the account not yet linked in signal-cli -> Connect spawns 'signal-cli -u N daemon', the daemon exits at once, the 90x1s listContacts probe fails, Connect silently falls back to subprocess mode (useDaemon=false, loadContactsSubprocess) and returns nil, so proto.Manager marks Signal StateConnected with no Warn logged. The user then links via the web UI; link.finalize persists the number and the SPA calls link.reconnect, but Manager.start skips slots in StateConnected/StateConnecting, so nothing restarts: /api/status reports signal:false, no daemon runs, the web UI shows no Signal tab until a server restart. Fix: (1) link.reconnect (core.Reconnect) must force a restart of the named backends (disconnect + connect) instead of skipping connected slots; (2) Signal Connect must not report success when the daemon died: log a Warn with the daemon exit status/stderr and either fail or retry once the account exists; (3) a contract/unit test for: boot with unlinked account -> link -> reconnect -> daemon up and backend_ready published.
notes:
Hand-off on worker/mc-tih, commit 514ca02 (9 files, +447/-32). Not pushed, bead not closed.

ROOT CAUSE (two layers): (1) proto.Manager.start skipped slots in StateConnected/StateConnecting, so Core.Reconnect (link.reconnect) was a no-op on a backend the manager believed connected. (2) signal.Connect spawned 'signal-cli -u N daemon'; with the account not linked the daemon exited at once, the 90x1s probe failed and Connect silently fell back to subprocess mode returning nil -> Manager marked Signal StateConnected with no Warn. After linking nothing restarted Signal, so /api/status signal:false until a server restart.

FIX:
- proto/manager.go: new Manager.RestartBackend(protocol) = Disconnect+Connect regardless of tracked state; Core.Reconnect uses it (Core.connect gained a restart flag; boot still uses StartBackend). start/connectOne now holds the per-slot restart lock around the skip check+Connect, so a restart can neither interleave with an in-flight connect nor start a second event pump; RestartBackend holds it across its Disconnect+state reset.
- proto/signal/backend.go: daemonProc records cmd.Wait result (exit status) and a 4KiB stderr tail; if the spawned daemon exits during the probe, Connect logs a Warn and returns 'signal-cli daemon exited (<status>): <stderr tail>', and stops the SSE listener started for it. Subprocess fallback kept (now with a Warn) only when the daemon is alive but not answering. Dropped the unused daemon *exec.Cmd field.
- core/core.go: 'check Signal: daemon attivo' only when b.IsConnected(); otherwise Python-parity 'warning Signal: daemon non disponibile (subprocess)'.
- proto/whatsapp/backend.go: Connect restarts the session guard when reconnecting (Disconnect stops it), so forced restarts cannot leave WhatsApp unguarded.
No app.go Build() changes, no config/.env changes.

TESTS (all new; both regressions verified to FAIL on the pre-fix code):
- core/reconnect_test.go TestReconnectRestartsSignalAfterBootDaemonFailure: real signal.Backend + fake CLI/HTTP RPC; boot with unlinked account -> failed status 'daemon exited' + backend_done, no backend_ready, StateFailed; link -> Core.Reconnect -> backend_ready, daemon up, StateConnected.
- core/reconnect_test.go TestReconnectForcesAStaleConnectedBackend: Connect-succeeds-while-dead backend in StateConnected; Reconnect must actually connect it.
- proto TestRestartBackendForcesReconnect: StartBackend still idempotent, RestartBackend disconnects+reconnects, ErrNoBackend for unknown.
- signal TestConnectFailsWhenSpawnedDaemonExits: error contains status 3 and stderr; IsConnected false. testdata fake CLI gained FAKE_SIGNAL_DAEMON_FAIL/EXIT.
- whatsapp TestReconnectRestartsSessionGuard: cold Connect leaves the app-owned guard alone; Disconnect stops it; Connect after Disconnect starts it again.

- cmd/megachatd/app.go Build(): register Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram only when enabled (Signal is no longer always registered); drop the Signal special case in core.WithAutoConnect if now redundant (check internal/core/core.go comments about 'Signal is registered always'). Describe the before/after of link.status for a fresh install in the hand-off note.
- Contract fixtures (tests/contract/harness.py, conftest.py): the harness pins SIGNAL_ENABLED=0 for Go today. Make every fixture state its flags explicitly; fixtures that need the real Signal backend registered (go_seeded window/snapshot over seeded Signal rows, test_parity) must opt in, e.g. SIGNAL_ENABLED=1 with no signal-cli present. Add a contract test: a Go server started with no flags exposes no chat backends and Gmail unconfigured (via the existing meta/status ops).

title: Default-off integrations: Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram, Gmail start only with explicit <X>_ENABLED
description: User request (2026-11-06): every backend of megachatd, including Gmail, must be OFF by default and turned on only by an environment-driven flag, like WHATSAPP_ENABLED. The shared spec and the worker protocol are in the design field; every child bead follows them.
design:
## Goal
Every integration of megachatd (the Go server) is OFF unless explicitly enabled:
Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram and Gmail. Today each has an implicit enable that must go away:

| Integration | Flag (env / .env) | config.json key | Implicit enable to REMOVE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Signal   | SIGNAL_ENABLED   | signal_enabled   | user number set (SIGNAL_USER_NUMBER / user_number); backend is also always *registered* today |
| WhatsApp | WHATSAPP_ENABLED | whatsapp_enabled | <data>/whatsmeow.db exists; WHATSAPP_API_URL set |
| Telegram | TELEGRAM_ENABLED | telegram_enabled | TELEGRAM_API_ID + TELEGRAM_API_HASH set |
| Gmail    | GMAIL_ENABLED    | gmail_enabled    | GMAIL_ADDRESS + GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD set |

## Shared rules (all four, identical)
1. Precedence: process environment > config.json key > project .env. A blank value falls
   through to the next source. Parsing is the existing lookupBool in
   megachatd/cmd/megachatd/app.go (1/true/yes/on, 0/false/no/off, case-insensitive);
   an unparseable value falls through. config.json accepts a JSON bool or one of those strings.
2. No flag anywhere => OFF.
3. OFF means not started at all: chat backends are NOT registered with the proto.Manager
   (exactly what WhatsApp already does when disabled); Gmail reports "not configured" and its
   unread watcher does not run. core.WithAutoConnect's Signal special case becomes redundant.
4. ON but required credentials missing (Telegram api id/hash, Gmail address/app password) =>
   not started, one Warn log naming the missing settings. Signal ON without a user number keeps
   today's Signal behaviour (it can still be linked through link.* ops).
5. Migration: when an integration is OFF but has evidence of earlier use (Signal user number,
   whatsmeow.db or WHATSAPP_API_URL, Telegram credentials, Gmail credentials) log one Warn and
   append one user-facing notice to App.Notices (same mechanism as WhatsAppRelinkNotice; Italian,
   like the existing notices) saying which <X>_ENABLED=1 to set in .env. Existing installs
   otherwise silently lose backends on upgrade.
6. The disabled log line for each integration names its flag, like the existing
   "WhatsApp backend disabled (enable with WHATSAPP_ENABLED=1 ...)".

## Out of scope
- The legacy Python server (MEGACHAT_SERVER=python: server/, protocols/) is NOT changed.
- No change to the wire contract (megachatd/CONTRACTS.md) unless a disabled backend already
  changes an observable reply; if so, document it in the hand-off note instead of editing the contract.

- Gates (run once, by you): cd megachatd && go vet ./... && go test ./... while iterating;

title: WhatsApp: unread badge can exceed the phone count for chats without an app-state markChatAsRead entry
description: Per-chat unread is reconciled from (a) history-sync UnreadCount, (b) on-demand history ingested read, (c) app-state markChatAsRead last-read cutoff. A chat with genuine unread but no markChatAsRead entry and no fresh history sync keeps every locally ingested historical message as unread (observed group with 235 unread locally; phone count unknown). Needs an authoritative per-chat unread source or a history resync trigger. Desired outcome: reconcile unread to an authoritative per-chat count or trigger a history resync so historical messages without a markChatAsRead entry do not inflate the unread badge. Files/functions: megachatd/internal/proto/whatsapp/history.go (reconcileChatUnread), events.go, appstate.go.

worker: root cause — unread reconciliation only ran while a phone signal was being applied: ingestConversation used the sync's UnreadCount once then discarded it, and a message-less conversation returned early before reconciling, dropping the count; FetchHistory/startup resync only ask the phone when the cache is sparse, so a chat with a full local cache and no markChatAsRead entry (WhatsApp compacts old read mutations) had no heal path — hence 235 bogus unread. Fix: record the phone's count with its boundary (chatMeta.UnreadTS/UnreadKnown), apply it for message-less conversations too, mark read only what an on-demand page actually delivered (pageTS, so newer genuine unread survives), fold store per-key unread per chat (new Store.UnreadCounts) and re-apply snapshots where local unread exceeds the phone's count, and — for chats with unread and no trusted count — request that chat's history from the phone once per chat per process (the bead's resync trigger). files: megachatd/internal/proto/whatsapp/{backend.go,history.go,send.go,history_test.go,helpers_test.go}. tests added: TestHistorySyncMessageLessConversationAppliesUnreadCount, TestReconcileUnreadAsksThePhoneForChatsWithoutASnapshot, TestOnDemandHistoryKeepsTheNewerUnread, TestUnreadSnapshotIsReappliedToLateHistory, TestUnreadHealAsksAndAppliesThePhoneCount (each verified failing with its part of the fix disabled). gates: go vet ok; go test -race ok (whatsapp re-run -count=1 12.3s, new tests pass individually); contract 589 passed/0 failed; pytest skipped: no python changed. follow-ups: freshest count is still bounded by the last history sync (whatsmeow exposes no unread API); a phone that never answers a heal request is retried only on the next process start.

Fix these in askUntrustedUnread (the new phone requests): (1) It fires one on-demand history request per chat for EVERY chat with unread and no snapshot, back to back, at startup. Bulk peer requests to the phone risk WhatsApp rate limiting; Python never did this.
